entry.title: OpenAI Hires Uber President Jill Hazelbaker as Chief Corporate Affairs Officer
entry.summary:
OpenAI has appointed a new executive to lead its corporate affairs division, recruiting Jill Hazelbaker from Uber to fill a leadership vacancy that has existed since the start of the year. Hazelbaker, who currently serves as Uber's president, will leave the ride-hailing company on Nov. 30 to join the artificial intelligence firm as chief corporate affairs officer.
The appointment is aimed at stabilizing a senior management team that has seen frequent turnover in recent years, particularly as the company faces market uncertainty regarding a potential initial public offering. Hazelbaker previously managed several high-profile crises at Uber, including the ouster of founder Travis Kalanick and the company's legal efforts to ensure California drivers were classified as independent contractors.

entry.title: Meta's New US Bond Sale Draws $58B in Orders Despite Higher Borrowing Costs
entry.summary:
Investors placed as much as $58B in orders for the $15B U.S. dollar portion of Meta's latest bond sale, providing roughly four times the coverage for the five tranches of debt. The social media company is preparing to complement the U.S. sale with its first euro-denominated offering, bringing the total targeted raise to between $20B and $25B. While demand remained high, Meta's borrowing costs have increased; the 30 year bonds in the current offering are priced at about 2.2 percentage points above U.S. Treasuries, which is 0.9 points wider than comparable notes the company issued in April.
The funding push comes as S&P Global Ratings revised Meta's credit outlook from stable to negative, citing risks that AI capital expenditures could top $225B in 2027 and result in a $71B free operating cash flow deficit that year. The agency affirmed Meta's AA- rating but warned that the company's leverage could exceed 1.0x by 2027. The debt offering is part of a larger capital-raising effort totaling nearly $120B, which includes a $60B at-the-market program and roughly $37.5B in common and preferred stock sales.
